Lesson 13.6 · 55 of 78 · 24 min · Verified 17 Jul 2026

Change impact, rollout and post-release control

After this lesson you can:
  • Assess impact across process, data, policy and operations
  • Design migration, training and rollback
  • Define production admission and monitoring

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. Impact is multi-dimensional
  2. Release safely
  3. Prove the outcome
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. Impact is multi-dimensional

Check journeys, in-flight cases, contracts, KFS, accounting, reports, partners, roles, controls, data retention, guides and Academy content. Identify irreversible decisions and external certification or notice needs.

2. Release safely

Define configuration and code versions, maker-checker promotion, migration rehearsal, cutover entry criteria, communications, support model, rollback point and data repair. Canary evidence informs independent human approval; AI cannot approve release or rollback.

3. Prove the outcome

Set early-life monitoring for volume, decision mix, referrals, errors, reconciliation, complaints and control exceptions.

Compare with baseline, investigate drift and record closure criteria.

Update canonical documentation and training as part of done.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-IT-GRC — Requirements, change and test evidence must support controlled, auditable processing.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability PLT-009 — Controlled promotion.
  • Capability PLT-015 — Release and incident communication.
  • Capability OPS-001 — Operational readiness.
  • Capability AIG-021 — Independent human release authority for AI-assisted delivery.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. Who may approve an AI-proposed production release?

  1. The proposing agent
  2. An independent authenticated human with authority
  3. Any developer
  4. The model owner automatically
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Release authority remains with an independent human.
